answer: Each PoA identity must complete a Wesolowski-verifiable sequence of modular squarings, with every result depending on the previous one; GPUs cannot parallelize a single chain to remove its elapsed-time delay. An attacker can run clones concurrently, but each added identity still requires computation and hardware, making Sybil creation costly rather than free. The tundra-to-summit journey evokes that per-chain bottleneck, while the quill records its proof—not a security parameter.
